## Overview Enable routed experts capture (R3) with pipeline parallelism in Model Runner V2 using the multiprocessing executor. With R3 enabled, the TP2/PP2 curve closely tracks the TP2/PP1 reference throughout the run. ### Performance Benchmark setup: two nodes equipped with NVIDIA H20 GPUs, with 128 concurrent requests. ## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Correctness-focused review of cbfab0c9ea, with AI assistance from Codex and three independent review agents.

No new confirmed correctness defect was found in the reviewed paths. The inline comments are specific regression-coverage requests, not claims of reproduced failures. The main invariant is that every stage contributes the same request's accepted token interval from the same execution step, in global layer order.

We traced stage-leader selection and globally indexed RPC replies, Multiproc/RayV2 aggregation, per-stage store capacity and lifecycle, terminal-prefill broadcasts, speculative-rejection feedback, and retention of snapshots/receive tensors until asynchronous copies complete. RayV2 inherits the Multiproc implementation; legacy Ray is explicitly rejected.

Validation on this exact head: 170 existing CPU tests passed across pp_utils, routed_experts_capture, aux_output_config, and auxiliary store tests. Additional CPU probes passed for uneven stage aggregation with TP leader selection, auxiliary-only terminal-prefill broadcast, and actual capturer construction/capture/snapshot/aggregation with layer partitions 2/3/2, offsets 0/2/5, uint16 expert IDs, and snapshot independence. These local probes are not included in the PR.

Limits: the CPU runs used an external environment-compatibility shim. Runner test collection was blocked by a missing local FlashMLA submodule. We did not run GPU multiprocess/NCCL or CUDA-stream validation, and the reported training/performance results were not independently reproduced. Source inspection and CPU probes therefore do not establish end-to-end asynchronous PP correctness. Please retain targeted coverage for the newly introduced invariants as outlined inline.

[Regression coverage] Exercise auxiliary-only terminal-prefill broadcasts

Please add a CPU regression with need_aux_output=True, particularly a final prefill with max_tokens=1. For a five-token prompt completing prefill with max_seq_len=6, the current helper correctly returns need_broadcast=True and need_sampled_mask=[False]; without auxiliary output it returns False/[False]. Non-last stages need the acceptance counts to publish terminal R3 even though there is no subsequent decode state to update. All current helper tests use the default False, so removing this new condition would leave them passing. Please retain both controls and cover a terminal-prefill row mixed with a decoding row. Our CPU probe passed; this is a request to preserve the behavior in the regression suite, not a report that the current branch is incorrect.

We traced stage-leader selection and globally indexed RPC replies, Multiproc/RayV2 aggregation, per-stage store capacity and lifecycle, terminal-prefill broadcasts, speculative-rejection feedback, and retention of snapshots/receive tensors until asynchronous copies complete.
